mentl/90ae4e2:
Before family 2 landed a line, one substrate fact killed
site-classification for the value graph: a spine cell is a word
pointing to a heap record, and the values the columns and env point at
are allocated during inference, interleaved with scratch, and
published later by pointer-write — so no extent bracket at the publish
site classifies them, and a per-decl reset would zero live pointees
under every column written that decl. Extent brackets are sound
exactly where the extent is the publish, which is why family 1 stands.
Three sound forms priced: nursery evacuation, columns-first, no reset.
Columns-first chosen as the Mentl-native form — the 5.2/5.5 arc moves
published facts into pages and flat buffers, making the image set
exist by construction. 4.3 pauses at 2a; 2b's fork and reset DEP-gate
on the column arc, and the DEP-gate is the next thing to build — the
arc is the plan's own next phase, not a stop.

Close the handler-residual seam, the crown's most-hit blindness face:
fn f(xs) with !WASI = each((x) => println(...), xs) falsely passed
because a handler's residual row rode HandlerKind's raw decl handle,
outside the scheme every install instantiates. The dig found three
stacked losses, each measured before believed. HandlerKind stored the
parse-placeholder config tparams at all three registration writes, so
any install-time read chased dead cells; it now stores the minted
tparams the arms bind. The handler-arm scope exited with an empty
signature keep, dropping the arms' config-fn edges at the completion
prune; its signature is the config cells plus the handle result, so
the exit now passes signature_free_roots(tparam_cells ++ [s_h]). And
an edge-only residual finalizes as an alias of the free config cell,
which a bound-row read answers pure on; the residual is now read as
the cell as an edge, resolve_row(mk_ef_open([], resid_h)), the shape
a scheme's row rides. residual_with_config_args completes it: each
CALLED config arg's row joins at the install, root-membership in the
residual's own edge set deciding which; labeled or arity-short
installs fall back verbatim.

declaration widens (Intern, StringTable, GraphWrite, EnvRead, and the
judge's BranchEnv + Consume + WasiThreads + DiagRegister rows, the

mentl/903cbc4:
src/lower.mn's lower_stmt_list used
  [lower_stmt(head)] ++ list_concat([], lower_stmt_list(tail))
The list_concat wrapper meant the recursive call was NOT in tail
position — each frame held the continuation, so deep stmt lists
(pipeline.mn with many handler decls, or any wheel module with
hundreds of fns) grew the wasm stack and exhausted it.

Restructured to Ω.3 buffer-counter form: lower_stmt_list_loop
threads (buf, count, i) tail-recursively, ls_extend + ls_set per
stmt, returns slice(buf, 0, count). One Alloc per stmt; O(N)
total; tail-recursive.

Drift modes refused:
- 11 (acc++[x] in loop): no — buffer-counter with ls_extend_to + ls_set
- 9 (deferred): no — full restructure, no peer follow-up needed
- 6 (foreign-fluency): no — Ω.3 IS the substrate per CLAUDE.md

Empirical: main+pipeline trap chain went from `lower_stmt_list →
lower_stmt_list → ...` infinite-stack-frames pattern to deep but
bounded recursion through nested fn-decl lowering (still hits
limits in pipeline.mn's many-handler case via lower_stmt's FnStmt
arm; that recursion is structurally distinct and is the next
substrate cursor — Hβ.lower.nested-fn-stmt-tail-call).
mentl/9008b3c:
Per the user directive "no more workarounds" + ULTIMATE MEDIUM
discipline: replace the buffer-counter abuse pattern with a real
Buffer<A> substrate distinct from List<A>.

Pre-substrate, transient list builders (cfn_walk in emit's
collect_fn_names, collect_top_level_fn_names) abused List<A> by
writing count back to offset 0 after list_extend_to. This conflated
capacity and count, causing O(N²) reallocation: every list_extend_to
read the now-small count and reallocated again. For wheel-scale
N≈20K closures this exhausted the perm cap and trapped at perm_alloc.

Buffer<A> separates the two concerns:
  type Buffer<A> = Buf(List<A>, Int)   // data, count (count <= data.len)
  buf_make(cap) -> Buffer<A>           // capacity slots, count=0
  buf_push(own buf, x) -> Buffer<A>    // amortized O(1) push
  buf_count(ref buf) -> Int            // logical fill
  buf_data(ref buf) -> List<A>         // underlying storage
  buf_freeze(own buf) -> List<A>       // slice to count, return clean List

Wheel-side: lib/runtime/buffer.nx defines the type + ops.
Seed-side: bootstrap/src/runtime/buffer.wat (Tier 2, record-tag 360)
mirrors with $buf_make / $buf_push / $buf_count / $buf_data /
$buf_freeze.

Refactored emit-side callers:
  $collect_fn_names: $buf_make(16) → cfn_walk_list(buf, lowexprs)
                     → $buf_freeze
  $collect_top_level_fn_names: same shape
  $cfn_walk + $cfn_walk_list: thread Buffer<String> through recursion;
                              push fn names via $buf_push (was
                              i32.store offset 0 + list_extend_to +
                              list_set + i32.store again)

Also reverted the heap-top in-place trick from $list_extend_to
(commit ebcae2c) — it was a workaround for buffer-counter abuse.
With Buffer<A> the abuse pattern is gone; list_extend_to returns
to its simple semantics (offset 0 = count, monotonic).
